paper_title: Search for axion-like particles through nuclear Primakoff production using the GlueX detector
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis labeled '1/Λ95 [GeV^-1]'
notes: Paper presents first search for ALP via Primakoff production on nuclear targets using GlueX detector. Mass range 200–450 MeV explored via X→γγ decay. Coupling limits on scale of O(1 TeV), i.e., 1/Λ ~ 10^-3 GeV^-1. Data extracted from Figure 7 (top, solid black line showing observed 95% CL limits). The paper reports limits as 1/Λ_95 in GeV^-1 units. Confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) numerical values read from plot rather than table, (2) background subtraction and systematic uncertainties (17% total) affect reliability, (3) paper notes observed limits fluctuate more than expected from background-only hypothesis, particularly a dip at 360 MeV. The background-subtracted limits (dashed red, Figure 7 bottom) are less stringent and show better agreement with expectations, but the nominal limits (solid black) are presented as the primary result. No DM density assumption applies (this is a collider/beam experiment, not a haloscope). The x-axis spans 0.20–0.45 GeV (200–450 MeV), and the y-axis spans approximately 1e-5 to 1e-2 GeV^-1 on a log-log scale. The boundary traced is the observed limit curve (solid red line), which shows a characteristic dip around 360 MeV corresponding to a downward fluctuation in the background-subtracted mass spectrum. The limit improves (decreases) from ~8.5e-3 GeV^-1 at 200 MeV to a minimum of ~2.2e-3 GeV^-1 near 450 MeV. The shaded grey region represents the ±1σ expected fluctuation band. Data points were sampled more densely near the dip feature (360 MeV) where the boundary changes slope most rapidly, and more sparsely in the smooth regions at lower and higher masses.
